title: Smriti Irani Says She Called for Work After 2024 Election Loss: 'I'm Unemployed'
excerpt: The former Union minister reveals she picked up the phone and asked JioHotstar's Uday Shankar for a job, leading to her return as Tulsi Virani in Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2.
body:
• Smriti Irani says she called Uday Shankar, Vice-Chairman of JioHotstar and Star, after her 2024 Lok Sabha defeat and told him she was unemployed
  • Shankar, who Irani credits with both ending and reviving her TV career, offered her the opportunity to return as Tulsi Virani
  • Irani lost her Amethi seat to Congress's Kishori Lal Sharma by over 1.67 lakh votes in the 2024 general elections
  • She has dismissed talk of political retirement, saying "Who retires at 49?" and hinting at an earlier-than-expected comeback in the BJP

Smriti Irani, who served as a Union Cabinet minister for nearly a decade before losing her Amethi constituency in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, has spoken publicly about the weeks that followed her defeat — and the phone call that brought her back to television.

In a recent interview with Times Now, Irani described reaching out to Uday Shankar, now Vice-Chairman of JioHotstar and Star, to ask for work. Shankar had been associated with television when her original show, Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, went off air.

"I picked up my phone and asked for a job in media and entertainment. I said I'm unemployed; can you give me something? He was the reason why I lost my job in the entertainment industry. Then, he also became a reason why I joined back."

— Smriti Irani, in interview with Times Now

A Cabinet Minister Asking for a Job

Irani recalled telling Shankar directly that she needed work. "I told him, 'Sir, I don't have a job. Can you help me?' At that time, Uday was overseas, and when he heard what I was saying, he asked me, 'Are you sure? You had been a Cabinet minister, and now you are asking for a job?'" she said.

Her response was matter-of-fact. "I said, I don't think there is anything wrong with returning to my professional field."

Irani acknowledged that her presence on set initially surprised the crew. "Everybody on the set was a little flabbergasted. People were wondering, how will I work with the daily wages?" she recalled. "Those who know the work understand this. You can work up to 12-hour shifts, and you are never really off the job."

From Amethi to the TV Set

The 2024 Lok Sabha elections had dealt Irani a decisive blow. She lost her Amethi seat — once considered a Congress bastion that she had wrested from Rahul Gandhi in 2019 — to the party's Kishori Lal Sharma by more than 1.67 lakh votes. The defeat, attributed partly to perceptions of local disconnect, was widely seen as the end of an era for Irani in Amethi.

But rather than retreating from public life, Irani moved back toward the career that had made her a household name. Produced by Ekta Kapoor, Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2 brought back the Virani family with Irani reprising her iconic role as Tulsi and Amar Upadhyay returning as Mihir Virani. The sequel has drawn strong viewership since its debut in 2025, fueled largely by nostalgia for the original show that dominated Indian prime-time television from 2000 to 2008.

No Plans to Retire From Politics

In a separate interview with Aaj Tak, Irani dismissed suggestions that her political career was over. "Why talk about 2029? Who knows what BJP will say in 2029? Why not 2026 or even 2025?" she said, hinting at an earlier return to active politics.

She pointed out that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi chose not to contest from Amethi this time. "In 2024, the Gandhi family refused to face me. I can't chase after them," she said.

"People talk about me during mayoral elections, assembly elections, and parliamentary elections — because my name is Smriti Irani. I have been an MP three times, served as a minister in five departments. Who retires at 49? People are just starting their careers."

— Smriti Irani, in interview with Aaj Tak

Irani has remained active in BJP organizational work since her defeat and appeared at Davos 2026 panels. She has described her current phase as that of a "part-time actor" who balances television with party responsibilities.

A Career Built on Reinvention

Irani's journey from television to politics and back has been marked by sharp turns. Born in Delhi, she grew up in financially difficult circumstances — her father sold books on the footpath and she worked at a fast-food outlet washing dishes before entering the Miss India pageant in 1998. Her breakthrough came in 2000 when she was cast as Tulsi Virani, a role that made her one of Indian television's highest-paid actresses.

She entered politics in 2004, contesting unsuccessfully from Chandni Chowk. After joining the BJP and winning a Rajya Sabha seat from Gujarat, she challenged Rahul Gandhi in Amethi in 2014, losing narrowly. She won the seat decisively in 2019, and served as India's youngest Cabinet minister in charge of portfolios including Human Resource Development, Women and Child Development, and Textiles.

Her return to television after the 2024 defeat, by her own telling, was not born of privilege but of pragmatism — a former minister picking up the phone and asking for a job.
